summary: Four soldiers died in a fire and explosion at CFB Wainwright on Saturday, and Albertans vote today on whether to start a path toward leaving Canada.
body: A fire and explosion during live training at CFB Wainwright in Alberta killed four Canadian Armed Forces members on Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said; the government says 39 were injured, and Global News reports 19 in critical condition [^1][^2][^3]. Carney called it one of the forces' worst peacetime tragedies on Canadian soil and ordered flags to half-mast [^2]. Military sources told Global News a munition likely started a grass fire, driven by gusts near 100 km/h, that led to the blast; the military says the cause is under investigation and there is no sign of terrorism [^1][^3]. Some military sources gave a higher death toll that officials have not confirmed [^1].

Albertans vote today, Oct. 19. Question 10 asks whether to stay in Canada or begin a legal process toward a future, binding referendum on leaving; a vote for the second option would not by itself make Alberta independent [^4]. Polls suggest about four in five Albertans want to stay, and many "leave" voters say they want to send Ottawa a message [^4]. Premier Danielle Smith, who opposes independence, is urging a yes vote on the nine other questions, such as limiting temporary residents' access to health care [^4]. Early results on Question 10 are expected tonight; polls are not results.
Also today, Statistics Canada releases September inflation. Forecasters expect 3.2%, ahead of the Bank of Canada's Oct. 28 decision, where the rate is expected to stay at 2.25% [^5].
differences: Accounts of the Wainwright toll differ: the government confirms four dead and 39 injured, while some military sources told Global News at least seven died [^1][^2]. On Alberta, Carney warns voters not to treat Question 10 as a way to "send a message"; some separatists say a strong showing is itself a message [^4].
